=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:359-428 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The cap-marker lookup reads only the newest 100 comments (`comments(last:100)`). When the trusted `review-autofix-failure-cap:v1` marker is older than that window, the function emits `kept/no_cap_marker` and the stale `ai:review-blocked` label stays.
  WHY: The evaluate-gate's own cap check reads the full comment history (.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1722), and the newly posted clean marker can make the gate skip later same-head reviews, so the label can stay indefinitely and the log gives no sign of it. Severity disagreement: openai_gpt-6-luna and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rated it MAJOR, mapped here to high. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT: in its view the behaviour is fail-safe, documented at lines 335-336, consistent with AD-1 option A, and the same-head skip is existing #8952 behaviour. Its only real concern is that `no_cap_marker` cannot be told apart from "marker out of window".
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:405-427 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: review_blocked_stale_clear() never checks whether the cap that wrote the marker labeled this PR. A cap on an older head that labeled only the linked issue can therefore cause a later `ai:review-blocked` label to be removed from the PR, even when a human or the review-blocked judge added that label.
  WHY: Issue #9369 says to keep the label when it "came from another path, such as the review-blocked judge or a human". The cap records which target it labeled ("Labeled `ai:review-blocked`: linked issue(s) #N" vs "this pull request (no linked issue found)", review_autofix.yml:1774-1787, 1811), but that text is not consulted. The trigger is narrow. The suggested fix of about 3 lines is to count a marker only when the same comment body contains "Labeled `ai:review-blocked`: this pull request".
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:review_blocked_stale_clear(), the embedded Python at lines 405-427 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The function never checks whether the cap that wrote the marker labeled this PR. The cap labels the linked issues when there are any, and labels the PR only when there are none (`.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` lines 1774-1787, comment at line 1811). So a stale issue-labeling cap marker returns `head_changed` and deletes a PR label that a human or the judge added later.
  WHY: Issue #9369 says to keep the label when it "came from another path, such as the review-blocked judge or a human". The trigger is narrow. Fix (about 3 lines): count a marker only when the same comment body contains "Labeled `ai:review-blocked`: this pull request".
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:line 359 `comments(last:100)`; line 428 `emit("kept", "no_cap_marker")` | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A trusted cap marker older than the newest 100 comments is reported as `outcome=kept reason=no_cap_marker`, the same reason logged when no marker exists at all.
  WHY: This is not a regression: the label is kept, which is the documented fail-safe (lines 335-336) and follows AD-1 option A. The gap is that the log hides the real cause. The reviewer declined the consensus MAJOR severity because the same-head skip is existing #8952 behaviour.
- HARDENING: scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:review_blocked_stale_clear(), DELETE branch `remove:head_changed|remove:support_changed`, around line 445
  PROBLEM: If the label is removed concurrently, the DELETE gets a 404 and the log says `outcome=error reason=delete_failed` even though the label is gone.
  WHY: Suggested fix: capture the DELETE's stderr and, on a 404 or "Label does not exist", log `outcome=removed` (or a new `already_absent` reason documented in the agents.d fragment). Estimated 4-6 lines.
- HARDENING: scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:line 360, `... > "${rbsc_response_file}" 2>/dev/null`
  PROBLEM: `2>/dev/null` hides the `::warning::` lines from `gh_retry`, so a `lookup_failed` result leaves nothing to diagnose it from.
  WHY: Suggested fix: drop the `2>/dev/null`, since `gh_retry` already redacts and escapes stderr. Estimated 1 line. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:359-360, 405-428 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The lookup reads only the newest 100 comments, then treats finding no cap marker in that window as `no_cap_marker` and keeps the label.
  WHY: If more than 100 comments have been posted since the trusted cap marker, the marker falls outside the query result. A clean review then leaves the stale label in place, and its clean marker can cause the gate to skip a later same-head review.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:lines 359 (GraphQL `comments(last:100)`) and 404-428 (newest-first walk emitting `no_cap_marker` when no trusted marker is found in the window) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The cap-marker search is bounded to the newest 100 comments, but the evaluate-gate's own cap check reads the full history (`gh api --paginate ... repos/${REPOSITORY}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments`, .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1722). A marker that has scrolled out of the window yields `kept/no_cap_marker`, and the new clean marker keeps the same-head gate skipping, so the stale label stays.
  WHY: This diverges from the linked issue's "Find the newest trusted cap marker" and the gate's paginate-everything convention, and the misclassification is silent. Mitigations: the failure is fail-safe, it is documented, it is constrained by AD-1, and the cap marker is realistically recent. The reviewer asks for an explicit decision: accept and document, or raise the window.
- HARDENING: scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:DELETE branch, case `remove:head_changed|remove:support_changed` (lines ~448-455)
  PROBLEM: A concurrent label removal makes the DELETE return 404, and the run logs `outcome=error reason=delete_failed` even though the label is gone.
  WHY: Suggested fix: treat a 404 as success (`already_absent` or `outcome=removed`) and document it in the agents.d fragment. Estimated 4-6 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
- HARDENING: scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:GraphQL labels fetch, line 359 (`labels(first:100)`)
  PROBLEM: A PR with more than 100 labels could miss `ai:review-blocked` and log `label_absent` while the label exists. Practically unreachable.
  WHY: No fix is required. If the comments window is ever widened, consider a `labels(first:1, query:"ai:review-blocked")` style lookup instead. Estimated 1 line. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 0
